text:
Last night's Integration Debt Night, hosted by Kestrelmoor at their Flatiron office, drew about 60 of us for a panel on the unglamorous part of AI: the plumbing.

Priya Raman-Holt (VP Platform, Tallowbrook) and Marcus Feldane (founder, Quillary) shared what they've seen.

→ Tallowbrook maintains 140 partner integrations with a team of three engineers. Priya: "We stopped building connectors one by one and started publishing a spec. Partners build to it now."

→ Marcus said agent pilots fail at the integration seam, not at the model. His team's rule: wire up data access before choosing a model.

→ A show of hands backed him up. About 40 of the 60 in the room said an agent pilot at their company had stalled on getting data access.

The best moment was a disagreement. Priya thinks partners should own their connectors. Marcus thinks the platform has to own them or quality drifts.

Where do you land: partner-owned or platform-owned?

Thanks to the Kestrelmoor team for hosting.
